content.text: DIGITIMES Insight: Intel, TSMC, Samsung converge on backside power — packaging becomes the next divide: The article excerpt reports accelerator package power rising from about 500W in the A100 generation to 3,500–4,000W for Rubin Ultra-class products expected in 2027. It attributes to Intel Foundry an estimate that increasing a compute package from 1kW to 5kW raises PDN I²R losses from 89W to 2,222W and reduces the input-power share reaching transistors from 66.0% to 41.8%. The article is paywalled, and the assumptions or original calculation are not visible. (time=2026-10-02T03:21:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

content.text: VLSI 2026: Intel 18A Platform Momentum from Devices to Routed Designs: Intel describes backside power as freeing frontside routing and reports Intel 18A routed-design results including about 11% area reduction, peak dynamic voltage droop below 10mV versus over 90mV on Intel 3, and a 5–6% frequency uplift or up to 15% power reduction. These are Intel-reported design results, not the package-level 1kW-to-5kW loss calculation. (time=2026-06-16 13:58 (page local time; timezone unspecified); cutoff=UNKNOWN).
